title: How To Choose HR Software for Small Business

HR Software for Small Businesses: Evaluate Your Options in 6 Steps

Choosing HR software for your business starts with understanding what the business needs now and what it may need as it grows. In this video, you’ll learn the six-step framework for evaluating HR software. The video also highlights capabilities to consider, including payroll and tax filing, compliance alerts, digital onboarding, benefits enrollment, time tracking, integrations, mobile employee self-service, and access to human support. For a deeper evaluation framework, read the complete guide to choosing HR software for small businesses. To compare HR technology and service options, explore Paychex HR solutions, including the connected Paychex Flex platform and Paychex WISE AI intelligence built into Paychex products.

0:01 Is your small business ready for HR software? And how do you avoid picking the wrong one? These six steps will help you answer both.

Step 1: Map your size

0:09 Step one: map your size today and where you’ll be in 12 months, because headcount changes the rules. Tracking things by hand usually gets shaky around the 10 to 15 employee mark.And once you average 50 full-time employees, ACA reporting applies, and FMLA generally covers employers with 50 or more. Planning your first out-of-state hire? That brings a new state’s tax and employment laws. So shop for the business you’re becoming.

Step 2: Name your pain points

0:36 Step two: name your top two or three pain points. Maybe it’s a past payroll error, benefits you’re offering for the first time, or an audit on the horizon. Or maybe it’s just your time. HR administration eats up roughly 7 to 12 hours a week. If your week looks like that and you still can’t say why turnover’s climbing or how long it takes to fill a role, your spreadsheet has had a good run. Fix those problems first and skip the shiny extras.

Step 3: Budget for the total cost

1:04 Step three: budget for the total cost of ownership, not just the sticker price. Vendors structure their quotes differently, so add up base fees, add-on modules, implementation, training, and integrations.

Step 4: List your non-negotiables

1:18 Step four: list your non-negotiables. Compliance usually tops the list, since federal wage and overtime rules cover nearly every employer, and every state adds its own. So look for payroll and tax filing that stays current, alerts when laws change, and digital onboarding. Add benefits enrollment, time tracking that flows into payroll, and integrations that grow with you. If an option misses a must-have, cross it off.

Step 5: Ease of use

1:45 Step five: test ease of use, the feature that decides whether your team actually adopts it. Can employees check a pay stub or request time off from their phone? If not, they’ll email you instead, and your new software isn’t saving you time. Then ask who picks up when something goes sideways: a help article, or a real person who knows your business?

Step 6: See it in action

2:07 And finally, step six: see it in action, using your real workflows. Ask the vendor to run your payroll, onboard a new hire, or approve a time-off request during the demonstration. Then talk to references your size. What works for 200 employees may not fit a team of 15.

How Paychex can help

2:25 So how does Paychex stack up against that checklist? Our HR packages let you start with what you need and add as you grow. Paychex Flex brings HR, payroll, and benefits into one platform, powered by Paychex WISE. It’s our AI engine backed by over 50 years of HR expertise that helps answer everyday questions and keeps you informed of regulatory updates. And when you need a person, our HR professionals are there to help.

Wrap up

2:53 Choosing small business HR software is a big decision, but with these six steps, you’ll know what to look for. The full guide and our HR packages are linked below. And don’t forget to hit subscribe for more HR guidance for your business.
